title: Ensuring Licensed Remittance Companies Fulfil Commitments
what_it_is: Ensuring Licensed Remittance Companies Fulfil Commitments

sections.label: Documentary evidence for remittances
sections.summary: Licensees must provide documentary evidence showing the recipient received the transmitted money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Licensees must also provide proper documentary evidence to show that the recipient has received the money transmitted.

sections.label: MAS complaints on failed remittances
sections.summary: MAS received fewer than 100 complaints in 2023 on alleged failed remittances, under 0.01% of total value remitted from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The number of complaints directly received by MAS in 2023 on alleged failed remittances, is lower than 100 and amounts to less than 0.01% of total value remitted from Singapore.

sections.label: Frozen funds to China
sections.summary: SPF received over 670 reports of funds remitted to China being frozen, and MAS temporarily suspended non-bank and non-card channels for transfers to China.

sentences.text: As of 15 December 2023, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) has received more than 670 reports of funds remitted to China being frozen.
To minimise risks to consumers remitting funds to China, MAS has decided to temporarily suspend the use of non-bank and non-card channels by licensees for money transfers to China.

sections.label: Samlit remittance licensee obligations
sections.summary: MAS says Samlit considered civil action, licensees must meet regulatory expectations, and MAS can fine or reprimand breaches, but Samlit discharged remittance obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the case of Samlit, we understand that they have considered some civil action as it is a civil matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If these remittance licensees – they are licensed under the PS Act, as I mentioned in my original reply – are found not to meet with the regulatory expectations, we will take action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: While MAS cannot compel the remittance companies on compensation, we have told them that they should treat their customers fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But if they are found to be in breach, we could take regulatory and enforcement actions, including fines and reprimand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But as I mentioned in my earlier response to the supplementary question, in this case, we found that they have discharged their obligations in terms of remitting, and this is an issue that MAS, SPF and the relevant Government agencies are engaging with the PRC agencies to resolve the matter.
